h1:
Chiang Mai Food
12 Dishes to Try
intro: Chiang Mai is a city you can eat your way through all day without repeating a thing — from a steaming bowl of khao soi in the morning to a mountain-coffee cafe in the afternoon. Here's what locals actually eat and what you shouldn't skip.

blocks.html: If it's your first time in Chiang Mai, the food is the reason a lot of people want to come back. The city has traditional northern Thai dishes, morning-market street food, and a new wave of cafes brewing beans from the hills around town. We picked 12 things that, once you try them, make it obvious why people get hooked.

items.name: Khao Soi
items.blurb: Egg noodles in a coconut-curry broth built on northern curry paste, topped with crispy fried noodles and served with chicken or beef. Eat it with pickled greens and shallots on the side. It's the dish people picture when they think of Chiang Mai.

items.name: Nam Ngiao with rice noodles
items.blurb: A lightly sour, orange-tinted broth (the color comes from dried cotton-tree blossoms) ladled over fresh rice noodles, eaten with crispy pork rinds and raw veg. It's a go-to breakfast for northerners.

items.name: Sai ua + pork rinds
items.blurb: Grilled herb-packed northern sausage, eaten on its own as a snack or with sticky rice. You'll find it at morning markets and souvenir shops all over town.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: The good khao soi often sells out before afternoon. If you've got a popular shop in mind, go before noon to be safe.

blocks.html: Chiang Mai is a serious cafe town, with hundreds of coffee shops pouring beans from the hills around it like Mon Jam and Doi Chang — everything from spots inside the old city to cafes out in the fields around Mae Rim and San Kamphaeng.

items.name: Cafes around Nimman
items.blurb: Design-forward shops you can hop between in one neighborhood — good for getting work done.

items.name: Field cafes in Mae Rim
items.blurb: Mountain and garden views, worth a drive out to sit and slow down in the morning.

items: Warorot Market (Kad Luang) — northern snacks, take-home treats and curry pastes, all in one place

faq.q: What are the must-try foods in Chiang Mai?
faq.a: Khao soi is the number-one dish people think of, followed by nam ngiao and sai ua, plus the northern set of dips like nam prik ong and nam prik num — and the mountain-coffee cafes that are a signature of the city.

faq.q: Where should I eat khao soi in Chiang Mai?
faq.a: Well-known khao soi shops are spread across both the old city and the Chang Klan area. Most open from morning until afternoon, so go before noon since a lot of them sell out fast.

faq.q: How much should I budget per meal for good food in Chiang Mai?
faq.a: Local dishes like khao soi, nam ngiao or a rice plate run around ฿40–70 a bowl. Street food and night markets are ฿30–60 a plate, while cafes and nicer sit-down spots are around ฿120–250 per person. Three relaxed meals in a day comes to roughly ฿300–500 per person and you'll eat well.
